title: Victim surveys and police records measure overlapping but different crime worlds
source_unit: Bureau of Justice Statistics comparison of the National Crime Victimization Survey and FBI National Incident-Based Reporting System

denominator.unit: persons for both comparable reported-to-police rates

ncvs_reported_to_police.unit: victimizations per 1,000 persons age 12 or older

measure_gap.unit: NCVS minus NIBRS rate points per 1,000

observations.method: BJS comparison aligning NCVS violent crime reported to police and excluding simple assault as closely as possible with FBI NIBRS estimates; source-specific definitions and populations remain distinct.
observations.uncertainty: NCVS interviews persons age 12 or older about experienced crimes and NIBRS counts incidents recorded by law enforcement. Crime definitions, covered populations, reporting completeness, reference periods, and estimation methods differ.
observations.subgroup: United States; comparison covers multiple crime types and 2022–2023 estimates, with separate person and household denominators by crime category.
observations.counterinterpretation: The rate difference is not a direct nonreporting rate, agency-performance rate, or victimization gap. It can reflect nonreporting, coverage, definitions, survey recall, agency reporting completeness, and included populations.

denominator.unit: households for NCVS and persons for NIBRS; not a common denominator

ncvs_property_rate.unit: victimizations per 1,000 households reported to police

denominator_boundary.value: not directly comparable as one rate

observations.method: BJS comparison table; property rates are retained with their original household versus person denominators.
observations.uncertainty: Because the denominators differ, the numbers cannot be subtracted or interpreted as a reporting share. NCVS excludes some populations and NIBRS includes crimes and populations not covered by NCVS.
observations.subgroup: U.S. households for NCVS property victimization and U.S. persons/crime incidents for NIBRS.
observations.counterinterpretation: A larger NCVS numeric rate does not establish more unrecorded crime without aligning units, populations, definitions, and reporting paths.

related_sources.claim: BJS describes NCVS as a survey of crimes experienced and reported or not reported to police.
FBI describes NIBRS as law-enforcement incident reporting.

boundary: This record adds a measurement boundary between victim experience and police-recorded crime. It does not establish a universal true crime rate, a reporting percentage, police performance, case resolution, safety, trust, or political response.
